push_back.description: Appends a copy of value to the end of the container, growing its capacity (reallocating and invalidating iterators/references) if needed.

pop_back.description: Removes the last element. Calling this on an empty vector is undefined behavior - check empty() first if the vector could be empty.

size.description: Returns the number of elements currently held, not the allocated capacity. O(1).

empty.description: Returns true if the vector has no elements. Prefer this over checking size() == 0 - it's the idiomatic form and works the same way across every standard container.

at.description: Bounds-checked element access: throws std::out_of_range if pos is invalid, unlike operator[] which is undefined behavior on an out-of-range index.

clear.description: Destroys every element, leaving size() == 0. Capacity is unspecified but typically unchanged, so it does NOT necessarily free the underlying allocation (use shrink_to_fit() for that).

insert.signature: iterator insert(const_iterator pos, const T& value)
insert.description: Inserts value before pos, shifting every following element - O(n) in the distance from pos to the end. Invalidates iterators at or after the insertion point.

erase.description: Removes the element at pos, shifting following elements down - O(n). Returns an iterator to the element that followed the erased one.

reserve.description: Pre-allocates capacity for at least new_cap elements without changing size(). Useful before a loop of many push_back calls, to avoid repeated reallocation.

front.description: Returns a reference to the first element. Undefined behavior if the vector is empty.

back.description: Returns a reference to the last element. Undefined behavior if the vector is empty.

duration_cast.signature: template<class ToDuration, class Rep, class Period> constexpr ToDuration duration_cast(const duration<Rep, Period>& d)
duration_cast.description: Converts a duration to another duration type, truncating toward zero (e.g. milliseconds -> seconds drops the fractional part rather than rounding).

steady_clock.description: A monotonic clock that never gets adjusted (no NTP jumps, no DST). Use this, not system_clock, for measuring elapsed time or intervals.
